newsitem.title: USA: 20 U.S. counties snare coveted AAA rating - S&P.
newsitem.headline: 20 U.S. counties snare coveted AAA rating - S&P.

text.p: A total of 20 counties in the U.S. were affirmed or upgraded to AAA due to diverse economies, strong financial management and low debt burden, Standard & Poor's Corp said Monday.

The top-flight AAA category, only one percent of all of the credit agency's ratings for general obligation debt, shows these counties have an extremely strong capacity to pay prinicipal and debt, it said.

Four counties in North Carolina were rated triple-A, followed by three in Virginia, and two each in Maryland, New Jersey and Georgia. Ohio, Texas, New York, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, and Illinois all have one county in this category.
All the ratings carry a stable outlook and Standard and Poor's said at present it sees no threat to their credit quality.

The group of 20 counties were measured according to a number of yardsticks, including overall net debt per capita, which ranged from a low of $770 for St. Louis, Missouri, to a high of $2,875 for Dallas, and general fund balance as a percent of expenditures, which ran from a low of 4.4 percent for Westchester, New York, to a high of a high of 105 percent for Kont, Michigan.
Unemployment rates in the counties were as low as 2.4 percent in Wake, North Carolina, to as high as 4.3 percent in Morris, New Jersey.
